title: Photosynthesis & Cellular Respiration — Fill in the Blank

questions.question: In a plant cell, photosynthesis takes place in the ___, an organelle whose green color comes from the light-absorbing pigment ___.

Inside a chloroplast, the light-dependent reactions happen across the ___ membranes, while the Calvin cycle happens in the fluid surrounding them, called the ___.
The Calvin cycle fixes atmospheric carbon using ___, an enzyme so plentiful it is considered the most abundant protein on Earth.
Glycolysis needs no oxygen and takes place in the ___, yielding a net gain of only ___ ATP per molecule of glucose.
The citric acid cycle — also called the ___ cycle — runs in the mitochondrial ___, the fluid enclosed by the inner membrane.
As electrons move down the electron transport chain, their energy pumps ___ ions into the intermembrane space; the flow of those ions back through ATP synthase is called ___.
In aerobic respiration the final electron acceptor is ___, and once it accepts those electrons it combines with hydrogen to form ___.
Deprived of oxygen, yeast ferments glucose into carbon dioxide and ___, while overworked human muscle cells instead accumulate ___.
ATP is the cell's energy currency; the abbreviation stands for ___.
A leaf exchanges gas with the air through pores called ___, each of which is opened and closed by a pair of ___ cells.
Capitalization matters in chemical symbols, so write these exactly: the gas photosynthesis releases is ___ and the gas it consumes is ___.
